title: Geometrically regular fibres after a Noetherian ind-etale pair colimit
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $c$ a colimit cocone in the under category of $A$ on the full subcategory of etale maps $A\to D$ for which $A/I\to D/ID$ is bijective [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. Write $B=c.\mathrm{pt}.\mathrm{right}$ and $f:A\to B$ for its structure map. Assume $B$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $C$ be a commutative ring and $g:B\to C$ any homomorphism. If $g\circ f$ is regular [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then for every prime $q$ of $B$, $\kappa(q)\otimes_B C$ with the algebra structure induced by $g$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(q)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. No flatness of $g$, henselian-pair hypothesis on $B$, G-ring hypothesis, or completion is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AH3, displayed product of completed fibres and following paragraph; the calculation applies to any B-algebra C. Uses Tag 0AH1 and Algebra Tag 07QH; checked on the Stacks tag pages.

proof.text: The pair-henselization indexing category is filtered. Transport the under-category colimit along the equivalence with commutative A-algebras. Apply the finite-separable-fibres theorem to B = c.pt.right: for p the contraction of q, the canonical A-algebra fibre is the finite product of the residue fields of all primes q_i over p, and each kappa(q_i)/kappa(p) is separable algebraic.

Tensor the finite product over B with C, with the B-structure supplied by g. Tensor cancellation identifies this tensor product with kappa(p) tensor_A C. Distribution over finite products identifies it with the product of kappa(q_i) tensor_B C. The q factor is the required fibre, and the isomorphism respects the kappa(p)-algebra structures. Binary tensor-product distribution iterated over the finite index set gives the product identity.

The regular composite makes kappa(p) tensor_A C geometrically regular. Its projection to the q component is localization at the idempotent with 1 in that component and 0 elsewhere: every element of the component lifts to the product, and the kernel is killed by that idempotent. This projection also makes the component Noetherian as a quotient. The same idempotent description survives every finite purely inseparable scalar extension. Apply regularity of localizations to each extended product to show the component is geometrically regular over kappa(p).

Use the compatible residue-field map kappa(p) to kappa(q) from the canonical decomposition. It is separable algebraic by step 1. The q component is Noetherian by step 3. Apply geometric regularity over a separable algebraic extension to conclude geometric regularity over kappa(q). Empty products present no prime q to check; zero factors remain regular by the vacuous prime-local criterion.

If B is a Noetherian filtered colimit of etale A algebras and A to C is regular, then fibres of B to C are geometrically regular

lean.statement:
theorem pair_henselization_regular_fibers
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (c : Cocone (ObjectProperty.ι
      (fun D : Under (CommRingCat.of A) ↦
        AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map D.hom) ∧
          Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map D.hom.hom) D.hom.hom
            (Ideal.le_comap_map)))))
    (hc : IsColimit c) [IsNoetherianRing c.pt.right]
    (C : Type u) [CommRing C] (g : c.pt.right →+* C)
    (hregular : (g.comp c.pt.hom.hom).IsRegular) :
    letI := g.toAlgebra
    ∀ (q : Ideal c.pt.right) [q.IsPrime],
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular q.ResidueField (q.Fiber C)
